content.comment_body: Hello, I'm seeking guidance on how to read input signals into a VB application and then determine which outputs should be activated or deactivated. My VB program is quite complex and too large to fit onto the [product_name] [article_no]. Is there a way to read inputs and write outputs from VB, possibly over the internet, even if that involves converting RS232 to TCP/IP? I would like to network multiple [product_name] modules. As a beginner with VB, any example would be appreciated. Thank you.

Hello [user_name], Although not exactly the same, a related issue has been discussed previously. Check out information on retrieving data from [product_name] modules; it might be useful in your case. Alternatively, consider using a different controller like [version_no]. With that, you can visualize values using OPC and build your own VB interface. Hope this helps. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], I reviewed the article and it does look promising, but I'm unsure about controlling outputs, since it's mainly focused on logging, not writing to outputs. Excel (DDE) is too slow and unstable for output control, while OPC is more reliable and faster. Switching to another controller isn't an option—there's already a [product_name] in place, and it's a specific [version_no]. My priority is to force outputs via a VB application or something similar. Ideally, a web page could do this, perhaps using VBA and a web editor. Would appreciate any help with this.

At this [url] you can download a demo version of the driver. Restrictions of the demo: It only supports [article_no], and saving is not allowed. If you are interested in purchasing the product, contact me and I can provide the purchase link.
Hi [user_name], Using the programming connector with a serial or USB cable, you cannot change outputs; you can only read IO and status information.

Hello everyone, The main challenge is controlling outputs rather than just monitoring them. Is it possible to set timer values or adjust counter values while the program is running? If so, I could create a program that manages outputs via counters or timers. Thanks.
Hello [user_name], Interesting idea, but it can't be done. To set date and time, the [product_name] module must be put in stop mode, adjust the time, and then returned to run mode. [user_name]

It appears the [product_name] operator device can modify some variables on the controller, including outputs, depending on the running program. If the screen can do this, an external device might as well by emulating that communication. For instance, it could imitate pressing certain function keys. I'm working on decoding the communication pattern between the operator device and logic module, similar to previous work with PC-to-logic module communication. Any tips or hints are welcome.

Hi [user_name], I discovered a straightforward method to monitor the communication protocol between [product_name] and the operator device using a PC's serial interface (9-pin). Set your interface to 19200,E,8,1 and connect: RS-232 Pin 2 (Rx) to Operator Device Pin 8 (RS485 +), RS-232 Pin 8 (CTS) to Operator Device Pin 3 (RS485 -), and RS-232 Pin 5 (GND) to Operator Device Pin 5 (GND).

Hello [user_name], Since you're working on real-time value reading between PC and [product_name] with the appropriate cable, I just need to monitor one counter value. Can your software facilitate this? I want to import the decimal value into a .NET application. Thanks and regards!

Hi [user_name], Could you explain how to read the value of a block using the [product_name]-PC cable? I'd like to monitor values from a .NET application. If you can help, I'd appreciate it. Thank you and regards.

It depends. If your counter block's value is stored as an analog mark on the [product_name] controller, the software allows it. My application can monitor PLC inputs, outputs, analog marks, digital marks, and shift register state. Regarding exporting values to .NET, it may be best to develop the entire solution on one platform, though two applications could communicate through files if necessary.

Hello everyone, This may be slightly off topic, but has anyone tried to simulate a digital input activation (e.g., I24), whether physically present or not, from a PC through the serial cable? This approach could make output control possible by setting logic like 'if I24 then Q3' in the [product_name] configuration software. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for a way to read inputs and also control outputs on [product_name] modules via PC applications, especially using VB and networking. However, direct output manipulation is restricted when using the programming connector or standard PC interface; only monitoring features are available. Efforts to bypass this include trying timers or counters, as well as emulating operator device communications, but documentation and official support for such advanced integrations are limited.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to do more than just monitor—they want reliable, fast control of [product_name] outputs from a PC application via standard or network-based connections.
